## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix the off-by-one in the release gate before merge: `approved` now rejects a release that has exactly the minimum number of approvals, which contradicts the module's stated contract.

## Changes
This pull request regenerates `aaa-generated/catalog.json`, renaming 1,500 `legacy-service-*` entries to `production-service-*` with ports moved from 10000–11499 to 20000–21499 and adding a top-level `review_note` string key. It also rewrites `healthy` in `services/registry.py` as `not failures` and changes the approval comparison in `zzz-release/gate.py` from `>=` to `>`.

## Critical
- zzz-release/gate.py:5 — correctness — Restore `>=` so the minimum approval count passes — With the default `minimum=2`, `approved(2)` now returns `False` because `return approvals > minimum` replaced `approvals >= minimum`. That contradicts the module docstring at line 1: "A release needs at least the configured number of approvals." The existing tests in `tests/test_release.py:11-16` check only 3 and 1 approvals, so they cannot detect this. — Every release with exactly the configured minimum number of approvals is blocked, which changes the gate's contract without notice. — Fix: Revert to `approvals >= minimum` and add an `approvals == minimum` case to `tests/test_release.py`.

- This review did not read every changed line of `aaa-generated/catalog.json` one by one (pinned diff lines 2234–8979). A pattern search across the whole diff found no changed line in that range other than the service-key and port renames.
